posts.title: Death toll at 270 as Nepal watches for a second flood
body: Nepal Police said 270 bodies have been recovered as of Thursday evening. The flood hit Timure in Rasuwa on Wednesday morning and ran down the Bhote Koshi into the Trishuli and the Narayani. Bodies have been found as far south as Chitwan.

826 people remain out of contact, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority says. Most, 644, are tourists, 517 of them foreign nationals. Another 85 are security personnel who were on duty in the flood zone.
Out of contact does not mean dead. Phone lines, power and internet are down across the valley and are coming back slowly.

A second flood is still possible. Chinese state media says a barrier lake has formed upstream of Gyirong Port, on the China side, where the original landslide blocked the river. Observation posts are going up there to watch for a new burst, and rain forecast over the next three days could slow the work of clearing it.

USGS first read the shaking as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake. On Thursday it said fresh analysis of the seismic waves and satellite images found no earthquake took place. The signal came from an ice and rock avalanche that fell into the Lhende Khola on the Tibet side, dammed the river, then broke.

Nepal's Army says more than 5,000 army and police personnel are now working the flood zone, from Nuwakot to Chitwan, and rescued 125 people on Thursday, including 20 foreigners. Prime Minister Balendra Shah travelled to Bidur in Nuwakot on Thursday with Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal to see the damage and meet local officials.

In India, the NDRF and the Sashastra Seema Bal have put rescue teams on standby in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. The NDRF says the Gandak, which the Narayani becomes downstream, could see higher water levels.
Keep off the banks of the Bhote Koshi, the Trishuli and the Narayani until officials say it is clear.

posts.title: Infrastructure damage put at Rs 200 billion, hydropower losses still being counted
body: Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal said damage to roads and bridges is around Rs 200 billion. He called it preliminary information.

That figure does not include energy infrastructure. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has ordered an immediate assessment of hydropower damage. In Rasuwa, 8 projects have been hit, 5 of them operational with a combined 236 megawatts, and 3 still under construction with a combined 342 megawatts. Nuwakot has lost access to 6 more projects, 4 operational at 123 megawatts and 2 under construction at 53 megawatts.
Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan are still being surveyed for road and building damage, so the Rs 200 billion figure is expected to rise.

The government has released Rs 1 billion to the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. The World Bank has separately offered up to Rs 25 billion in emergency assistance, its Nepal country director told the finance ministry. That is aid, not a damage estimate.
Insurers say claims will take weeks to settle because most of the damaged sites cannot be reached by road.
